Real Estate Development Project Manager and Architect
														
																
																			CO-

												San Francisco, CA, USLocation:
						Mon, Nov 23 '26Posted on:
													Full-timeType:									
						                        
					 
				 
				
CO- (Collective Operations) seeks a Real Estate Development Project Manager and Architect on a full-time basis. CO- practices Architecture, Urban Design, and Real Estate Development in parallel and pursues equilibrium between design excellence and project feasibility. Current development work includes new construction and rehabilitation projects for multifamily housing in California.
The role will lead the project management, design development, construction documentation, and delivery of large multifamily projects. The individual will manage the internal team, coordinate consultants, and ensure the project advances at a high level of quality and efficiency. We are seeking an experienced Architect or Project Manager dedicated to the Real Estate Development field. We do not expect applicants to have significant real estate development experience upon application, but the successful applicant will be required to learn and take on real estate development responsibilities as part of the job.
Qualifications
- California Licensed Architect (preferred, not required)
- 3–5 years of professional experience
- Strong design abilities and judgment
- Highly organized, detail-oriented, and accountable, with strong project management skills and the ability to structure their own work independently while incorporating team feedback.
- Clear, proactive communication, coordination, and interpersonal skills for both internal and external relationships. Strong visual communication skills are beneficial.
- Experienced with new construction multifamily projects through construction documentation and administration, including preparing ASIs and RFIs, and reviewing submittals. Must have familiarity with Procore.
- Ability to interpret zoning and building codes (IBC + California addendum) and local jurisdictional requirements in preparing construction documents.
- Experienced in coordinating with engineering and consulting teams and navigating the building permit approval process with local jurisdictions
- High proficiency in Revit, Adobe, Rhino, and emerging AI workflows; working ability with Microsoft Excel.
- Rehab project experience, financial modeling experience, and/or familiarity with public funding mechanisms for affordable housing in California are a plus.
Job Responsibilities
- Primary responsibility from January 2027–June 2027 is to lead a large-scale project that involves surveying and documenting a portfolio of properties across the state. The work requires occasional travel and production of a summary report by mid-2027.
- Manage real estate development project schedules and budgets
- Underwrite new development projects and update financial proformas
- Coordinate with local jurisdictions on securing the required entitlements for new projects
- Work to secure financing commitments from public and private lenders
- Project manage development projects from acquisition through construction loan closing, construction, permanent loan conversion, and lease-up.
- Lead the project’s design development and construction documentation phases, ensuring quality, consistency, and code compliance
- Manage and coordinate consultants (structural, MEP, civil, landscape) throughout the CD/CA phases
- Review and interpret zoning/building codes and apply them effectively
- Respond to RFIs, coordinate submittals, and support construction administration
- Prepare and manage drawing sets, details, and specifications
- Collaborate with Partner-in-Charge on client communications and city meetings
- Attend and conduct site visits, documenting progress
- Track project schedules, deadlines, and milestones
- Maintain clear, organized project documentation
- Lead QA/QC reviews before issuing
- Prepare and submit permit packages, tracking approvals
- Lead technical detailing efforts with the team
Benefits
- Hybrid schedule: 3–4 days/week in San Francisco office
- Paid Time Off
- Sick Leave
- Health insurance and retirement
- Professional development support and licensure support
- Opportunity to work within CO-’s development wing, providing exposure to the development and finance side of projects
- Growth potential within the firm
- Team culture valuing balance, quality, and meaningful work on impactful projects
 
Applicants should apply directly through our online portal.
